Hi Olivia,

Great conversation today — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial: 

Call recap
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for in-prod latency (95th P99 under 250ms target), token-cost impact at expected QPS, and reliability under burst traffic for the seasonal promotion.
- Users: Crestview retail API (search & product recs) will call Redwood; Sam Park will own DevOps integration.

Proposed POC structure (high level)
1) Duration: 3 weeks of active testing after integration (2 weeks integration + 3 weeks trial ramp)
2) Success criteria (initial suggestions)
   - Latency: 95th <= 250ms for 99% of test windows
   - Availability: >= 99.9% for trial period (excluding agreed maintenance windows)
   - Cost: <= projected token spend budget (we'll model tokens for sample traffic)
   - Quality: end-to-end pass rate on the 30 prompt set (we'll include sample prompts)
3) Observability: dashboards for 95/99 latency, per-route token cost, token count distribution, error rate, KV cache hit rate, and tail latency traces. We also recommend exporting logs to your Datadog/Cloud Logging for longer retention.

Attachments: I attached a one-page scope workbook (crestview_poc_scope.xlsx) with the proposed timeline and roles.

Questions / asks for you
- Confirm Sam (DevOps) as the tech owner for integration and the contacts for procurement for contracts/PO?
- Any additions or changes to the success criteria above?
- Preferred dates for integration kickoff (we're tentatively proposing Aug 9 start).

I'll loop in Karthik for the trial plan and Ben for the integration/telemetry spec once we get a confirmation.

Thanks,

Hi Olivia, Vanessa —

Thanks — based on Vanessa's recap and Olivia's clarifications, here's a concrete POC acceptance plan and timeline that our team can commit to. This is focused specifically on observability/telemetry so you can validate performance and cost.

POC acceptance plan (detailed)
- Week 0 (by Aug 2): integration checklist completed, IAM keys provisioned, Datadog ingestion endpoint confirmed, PO/trial contract terms signed (if procurement moves fast).
- Week 1-2 (Aug 9 start): integration and smoke test
   - Redwood provides: SDK/inference client + sample integration script, prebuilt tracing plugin for your APM, and a Prometheus metrics exporter.
   - Benchmarks: run a 1k QPS smoke window and collect baseline telemetry.
- Week 3-5 (trial ramp): production-like traffic ramp with guarded canary and rollback policies
   - Observability deliverables:
     * Dashboards: latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), per-route token cost, token distribution histogram, error rate by error class, KV cache hit/miss rate.
     * Traces: end-to-end trace correlation IDs with downstream service spans.
     * Logs: structured JSON logs for requests that include request_id, model_variant, tokens_in/tokens_out, and response_time_ms.
     * Exports: daily token usage CSV to your S3 or email; Datadog metric export for central ops.
- Acceptance gates (end of trial):
   1) Latency gate: 95th <= 250ms for 90% of evaluation windows
   2) Error gate: less than 0.5% unhandled errors for trial windows
   3) Cost gate: token cost within 10% of projection for sample traffic
   4) Data & logs: telemetry streams available in Datadog and daily token CSV delivered to your finance inbox

Owners
- Redwood: Karthik (trial lead), Ben (integration & telemetry engineering)
- Crestview: Sam Park (DevOps), Olivia Hayes (product/stakeholder)

I'll attach a simple telemetry schema and Prometheus/Datadog mapping that Ben prepared (telemetry_schema.yaml). If this looks good, we can lock the Aug 9 kickoff and schedule a 30-minute tech sync next week to go over credentials and the exact dashboard widgets.

-karthik

Olivia / team —

Attached are the artifacts we discussed: 1) telemetry_schema.yaml (field-level mapping and export paths) and 2) crestview_poc_dashboard_sketch.pdf (PNG/PDF mock of the dashboards). Below is a concise spec for the telemetry items we will surface during the POC.

Telemetry spec (high level)
- Metrics (prometheus-friendly):
  * redwood_inference_request_count{route,model_variant,status}
  * redwood_inference_latency_ms{quantile,route,model_variant} (we'll ship histograms for p50/p95/p99)
  * redwood_inference_token_in_total, redwood_inference_token_out_total (per-route counters)
  * redwood_inference_kv_cache_hit_ratio{route}
  * redwood_inference_errors_total{error_type}

- Logs (structured JSON):
  * Fields: timestamp, request_id, user_id (if provided), route, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, response_ms, status_code, error_message
  * Export: push to Datadog Logs via HTTP intake or to S3 (for archival) — your preference.

- Tracing:
  * OpenTelemetry-compatible spans with an instrumented span for the Redwood inference call. We will correlate using request_id and include the model_variant as a span attribute.

Dashboards (minimum set)
1) POC Overview: total requests, success rate, average tokens per request, daily token spend estimate
2) Latency heatmap: p50/p95/p99 by route and by hour
3) Cost impact: per-route token histogram and cumulative spend (daily/weekly)
4) Errors & Exceptions: error rate by class with sample logs panel (latest 50)
5) Cache effectiveness: KV hit ratio and effect on latency

Retention and export
- Short-term: metrics/alerts retained in Datadog for 30 days for rapid debugging.
- Logs: 90-day retention, with nightly S3 archive (as Olivia requested).

Alerting suggestions (trial)
- Latency Surge: alert when p95 increases >30% vs baseline for 5 consecutive mins
- Error Spike: alert when errors_total increases >0.5% absolute over baseline
- Token Burn: alert when projected daily token spend > 120% of expected budget

Next steps
- If this spec works, I'll schedule a 30-min tech sync (Ben + Sam + Karthik + one infra engineer from Crestview) to confirm Datadog credentials and a temporary service account.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
